column1: HEBREW 1020 - INTRO TO MODERN HEBREW LANG
column2: Course Description: This course is an elementary course for students who have never studied the Hebrew language or those who have not studied it beyond grade six. The course is designed to teach students the alphabet, basic grammar, syntax, and vocabulary. Course material will build basic oral and written comprehension.Antirequisite(s): Grades 7-12 Hebrew or equivalent.Extra Information: 4 hours.

Course Description: An introduction to the writing system and grammar of Biblical Hebrew for those with no previous knowledge of the language. Special attention will be paid to the noun, adjective, and participle.  Antirequisite(s): Hebrew 1030 or Grade 4 Hebrew (or Grade 2 in Israel). Extra Information: 4 hours.

column1: HEBREW 1041B - INTRO TO BIBLICAL HEBREW II
column2: Course Description: Continuation of Hebrew 1040A/B. An introduction to the grammar of Biblical Hebrew for those with little previous knowledge of the language. Special attention will be paid to forms of the verb.  Antirequisite(s): Hebrew 1030 or Grade 6 Hebrew (or Grade 3 in Israel).Extra Information: 4 hours.

Course Description: This course is designed to build upon skills in reading and speaking modern Hebrew, developed in earlier courses. Students will gain increased vocabulary, and a greater understanding of more complex grammatical structures. Extra Information: 4 hours.

Course Description: Reading, translating, and analyzing the grammar of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible with the aid of a lexicon. Antirequisite(s): Grade 7 Hebrew (or Grade 4 in Israel).Extra Information: 4 hours.

Course Description: This course aims to build on the skills learned in Hebrew 2200 to improve students’ competency in oral and written Modern Hebrew. Exposure to a variety of materials, including literature, poetry, articles, and films, will enable students to develop oral and written fluency.Extra Information: 4 hours.
